records.title: Hypoxia Training: Symptom Replication in Experienced Military Aircrew
records.locator: Aviation, Space, and Environmental Medicine 83(10), Methods pp. 963–964 and Results p. 965
records.evidence_note: Twenty-six Royal New Zealand Air Force aircrew took refresher altitude-chamber training and paired hypoxia questionnaires; the average interval since previous training was 4.5 years. The authors adapted the Smith questionnaire and describe a separate population. Clinical DCS/AGE and inside-observer person-exposures were not tabulated.

records.title: Hypoxia Symptoms in Military Aircrew: Long-Term Recall vs. Acute Experience in Training
records.locator: Aviation, Space, and Environmental Medicine 79(1), Methods and Results p. 55
records.evidence_note: The Dhahran Armed Forces Aeromedical Centre distributed questionnaires to 58 eligible military aircrew; 49 returned paired questionnaires. The results measure recall and acute symptoms of hypoxia. The sample cannot supply the risk set for the separate arterial gas embolism case reports from the centre.

records.title: Serum Aminotransferase Alteration Following Altitude Chamber Experience in Military Aircrew
records.locator: Journal of Archives in Military Medicine 2(1) e17035, §§ 3.1–3.3 and 4
records.evidence_note: The authors assayed AST and ALT in 37 healthy male Iranian military aviators before and after altitude-chamber training. The introduction discusses DCS and inside observers in general. Methods and Results provide no clinical event surveillance or observer risk set.

records.title: Hypoxia and Time of Useful Consciousness in Hypobaric Chamber at 25,000 feet in Aircrew at dr. Saryanto Health Institute of Aeronautics and Space
records.locator: The Indonesian Journal of Occupational Safety and Health 13(2), Methods pp. 174–175 and Table 2 p. 175
records.evidence_note: The authors sampled 99 medical records of male active aircrew training in 2021 at Lakespra dr. Saryanto. Table 2 tabulates 62 with hypoxia symptoms and 37 without. Chest pain and tingling appear under nonspecific symptoms. The report does not ascertain clinical DCS, AGE or inside-observer outcomes.

records.locator: Jurnal Kesehatan Indonesia 16(1), Methods p. 51, Table 4 p. 52 and Discussion/Conclusion p. 54
records.evidence_note: The authors sampled 97 of 147 male military aircrew records. records.title: Septal deviation and other factors increase the risk of barotitis media in high altitude high opening training
records.locator: Medical Journal of Indonesia 17(1), Methods p. 38 and Tables 1 and 3 pp. 39–40
records.evidence_note: After a chamber training simulation in May–July 2007, 100 of 177 participants had otolaryngologist-confirmed barotitis media. The paper reports 78 of 125 trainees and 22 of 52 qualified flight engineer/freefall participants. The qualification group was exposed as participants. These are otologic diagnoses and the source supplies no clinical DCS or observer rate.

records.title: Hypoxia: An Analysis of Hypobaric Chamber Training
records.locator: ASU thesis, pp. 21–22 (training risks), p. 26 (Participants) and Chapter 4 (survey Results)
records.evidence_note: Of 123 responses, 110 were included in the survey on hypoxia and training perceptions. Recruitment used the ASU chamber course, industry social media and a newsletter. The 0.64 per 1,000 and 78 per 111,674 DCS numbers in the literature review are attributed to Piwinski et al. and Bason and Yacavone, respectively. They do not count events among the 110 survey respondents.
